functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The only suboccipital muscle with no attachment to the skull -- it runs between two vertebrae, and is the principal rotator at the atlanto-axial joint. The greater occipital nerve crosses its lower border, which is the landmark used for its block.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe over the suboccipital triangle, following the muscle's course from the C2 spinous process obliquely superolaterally to the transverse process of C1; identify it as the floor of the suboccipital triangle, deep to semispinalis capitis.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to semispinalis capitis and trapezius; the vertebral artery runs immediately superior/medial to the muscle as it curves toward the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: The greater occipital nerve winds around the inferior border of the muscle (cadaveric mean ~52 mm inferior to the external occipital protuberance, ~30 mm lateral to the midline) before ascending in the plane between obliquus capitis inferior and semispinalis capitis -- a useful confirmatory landmark on ultrasound.
structures_at_risk: vertebral artery (crosses just superior/medial to the muscle near the C1-C2 level)
greater occipital nerve (winds around the muscle's inferior border)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: In a cadaveric comparison of 9 pairs of cervical muscles, ultrasound-guided injection accuracy in obliquus capitis inferior was the lowest of all muscles tested (41.7%), because injectors deviated too far medially trying to avoid the vertebral artery; non-guided (palpation-only) injection was markedly less accurate than ultrasound guidance overall (48.0% vs 88.2%, pooled across all 9 muscle pairs). A per-muscle non-guided accuracy figure for obliquus capitis inferior specifically was not given in the available text.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Kreisler A, Gerrebout C, Defebvre L, Demondion X, 'Accuracy of non-guided versus ultrasound-guided injections in cervical muscles: a cadaver study', J Neurol 268(5):1894-1902 (2021), doi:10.1007/s00415-020-10365-w -- dye/gelatin/contrast injected into 9 pairs of cervical muscles across 11 cadavers, compared ultrasound-guided vs non-guided accuracy on frozen slices. Retrieved via PubMed. Danger-structure position from Kim HS, Shin KJ, O J, Kwon HJ, Lee M, Yang HM, 'Stereotactic topography of the greater and third occipital nerves and its clinical implication', Sci Rep 8(1):870 (2018), doi:10.1038/s41598-018-19249-6 -- 30 cadavers (60 sides), 3D-digitizer mapping. Retrieved via PubMed.

trigger_points.location_description: Deep, between the C2 spinous process and the C1 transverse process, through semispinalis capitis.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Suboccipital region and lateral upper neck, part of the 'inside the head' pattern.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
